Messages.Author: adam....@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Can you multirush wtih Eternal Vigilance or Imperial decree (assuming
rushing different vampires)? Or does it follow the no repeat action
rule?

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


EV allows a block attempt, not a rush.

Imperial Decree is a card in play, so is restricted.
http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/rulebook.html#sec6_1_6

Messages.Author: XZealot
Messages.Body:
On May 8, 9:26 am, "adam.hu...@gmail.com" <adam.hu...@gmail.com>
wrote:

> Can you multirush wtih Eternal Vigilance or Imperial decree (assuming
> rushing different vampires)? Or does it follow the no repeat action
> rule?

I assume you mean Covenant of Blood (the Non-Camrilla version).

Each copy of Covenant of Blood/Imperial Decree creates it's own action
so you could potentially place two copies of Covenant of Blood into
play and use EACH copy to generate its own rush action for multi-
rushing.

Messages.Author: Bram Vink
Messages.Body:


I think the intended question is a bit more complex.
I'd assume the following is meant:

I have one copy of Covenant of Blood in play.
I have a vampire that can use the action provided by covenant of blood
and this action has 2 distinct targets.
After taking an action per Covenant of Blood to rush my first target,
I untap.
Is is legal to now use the same Covenant of Blood to rush my second
target, assuming said target is still around?

-----
Covenant cardtext:
Requires a ready Non-Camarilla vampire with a capacity above 7. Put
this card in play. Any non-Camarilla vampire may enter combat with any
Camarilla vampire controlled by another Methuselah as a (D) action.
Any vampire may burn this card as a (D) action; Camarilla vampires get
-1 stealth when attempting that action.
-----
Relevant rulebook text: (6.1.6)
"A minion cannot perform an action with the same action card or via
the same card in play (including from the minion's own card text) more
than once each turn, even if he untaps"
-----

So: the answer is no. You cannot rush two different targets through
the action provided by a single card in play, regardless of target.

The quoted text in the rulebook doesn't even take into account wether
a different target makes an action distinct from the same action with
another target. The reason why he cannot take these two actions is
because they would provided by a single card in play.

Cheers,
Bram

Messages.Author: XZealot
Messages.Body:


Your English gets worse and worse.

There are two distinct questions which are phrased in a manner to
assume mutual exclusivity of the answers, but in fact, the answers are
not mutually exclusive. There is a condition that can be met where
both of the answers are yes.

"Can you multirush wtih Eternal Vigilance or Imperial decree (assuming
rushing different vampires)? "

"Or does it follow the no repeat action
rule?"

The answer is yes you can multirush with imperial Decree (provided
there are multiple copies in play). and yes it does follow the no
repeat action.
